items.title: The decomposition of the pushforward of the intersection cohomology sheaf of the regular part of a quiver variety
items.author: Hiraku Nakajima
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 5 (2009) article 003, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2009.003; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the branching theorem of the paper (author Theorem at source lines 2714-2731, label thm:branch): the pushforward of the intersection cohomology sheaf of the regular part of a quiver variety decomposes into a direct sum over v' of the Hom space between an irreducible integrable highest weight module of the Levi subalgebra and one of g, tensored with the IC sheaf of the regular part of M_0, plus IC sheaves of non-regular strata. The proof (source lines 2733-2803) is the paper's main technical argument: it first identifies the local-system decomposition of the top-degree homology of the fibre on the regular strata of both moduli spaces, using that the homology there is an irreducible integrable representation with a prescribed highest weight vector (proof lines 2734-2755), then rewrites an arbitrary stratum containing a given IC sheaf as a product stratum and pushes the exterior product through two finite birational morphisms, which is what forces all remaining summands to come from non-regular strata unless the second factor is trivial (proof lines 2757-2776), and finally reads off the restriction identity and identifies the multiplicities with the Hom spaces, using that the summands for different v^0 are non-isomorphic (proof lines 2777-2803). The argument is a chain rather than a single trick, and its middle step is the finite-birational-morphism computation. H2.
